newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia faces AIDS epidemic - health expert.
newsitem.headline: Russia faces AIDS epidemic - health expert.

text.p: The number of people infected with the HIV virus is rising sharply in Russia, especially among drug addicts, and the country faces an AIDS epidemic, Itar-Tass news agency said on Tuesday.

It quoted a coordinator of Russia's AIDS control programme, Mikhail Narkevich, as saying the number of newly registered HIV carriers in the first 10 months of 1996 was equal to the total incidence of the virus since the disease was first reported in the former Soviet Union in 1987.
"The number of infected people is growing at such a rate that it is possible to speak of the start of an AIDS epidemic in this country," Tass quoted Narkevich as saying.

Carriers of the human immuno-deficiency virus (HIV) that causes AIDS number around 2,081, while 245 people have the full-blown disease. Some 60 people are estimated to become infected with the HIV-virus every day, Narkevich said.

The figures are still low by international standards -- Russia's population totals 150 million -- but medical experts say they could grow fast because there has been a sharp increase in sexually-transmitted diseases.
Last year, the number of syphilis cases in Russia doubled.
Narkevich said he was alarmed by the trend among drug addicts, where registered HIV carriers now number 750 against just three at the start of this year.

The Russian parliament has passed a law demanding strict measures to stop foreigners bringing AIDS (Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome) into Russia, including a requirement for long-term visitors to prove they do not have HIV.
However the law has not been implemented.
The spread of AIDS in Russia was slowed by the country's relative isolation, conventional sexual behaviour and low drug abuse levels before the 1991 collapse of the Soviet Union.
